blocks.text: Hi Sandra,
One more item to go with Michael's note. He asked that any reporter who contacts {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} directly be passed to us, and we would like to make that easy for whoever takes the call.

Once outreach starts next week, some reporters will ring your main line or one of your sites instead of calling us. I am putting together a one-page media inquiry protocol for this, which I will label v1.

It will cover who takes the first call, what they say, and how the request reaches you and us the same day. To draft it properly, it would help to know which team answers your main line, and who covers for you when you are out of the office.
If you can send that over, we will have v1 with you early next week. We know this lands on top of everything else on your desk, so we will keep it short.

Best,
Laura
Hi Sandra,

Laura's protocol covers the first phone call, and the people who pick up that call will also need to know what not to say, so I would like to settle the protocol and the preparation session for your spokespeople together, particularly as the first pitches go out this week and any reporter who responds will want an interview soon after.

To fix the session date, as I said we would on this thread, three things from your side would help:
1. A half day next week when your spokespeople can be in one room with Laura and me, ideally a morning at your offices, because practice interviews work better in person than over video.
2. A short note on anything {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} expects to announce over the summer, or that customers or employees may already be talking about, so that the protocol can carry a holding line for it.
3. Your view on whether the front desk and site reception staff should sit in on the first hour of the session, which covers taking a message from a reporter and nothing more.

Once we have the date, Laura will send the agenda and the Q&A document the spokespeople will practice from, and Kimberly will put together a short summary of recent coverage of your sector for the room.

Sincerely,
Michael
Hi Sandra,
The media inquiry protocol is ready for your review. You will find it in the shared project folder as "Media Inquiry Protocol v1", on a single page as promised.

What we are asking you to approve is the routing at the top of the page: a reporter's call to {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} is logged by whoever answers it, passed to you, and sent on to us within the hour. The two holding lines underneath are drafts, and we expect you will want to adjust the wording.

I have left the team that answers your main line blank for now, so we can fill it in once we hear from you. On Michael's question, a morning at your offices suits us well, and we will bring copies of the protocol in case the front desk staff join us.
Separately, the first pitches will reach you later today, each in the form the reporter will see.

Best,
Laura
Hi Sandra,

Thank you for sending back your changes to the protocol and for confirming next Tuesday morning at your offices for the preparation session; Laura has folded your edits into the protocol as v2, and that is now the version your front desk and site reception teams should work from.

So that everyone on both sides is working from the same plan, this is how the session and the days around it will run:
1. Laura and I will run the session on Tuesday, with the first hour open to your front desk and site reception staff as you suggested, and we will need a room with a screen and a phone we can use for practice calls.
2. Melissa is checking the Q&A document against what {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} has said publicly over the past year, so that nothing we ask your spokespeople to say goes further than earlier statements, and she will have that done before Tuesday.
3. Kimberly will send the first weekly summary this Friday, covering the reporters contacted, the replies so far, and anything from our monitoring that deserves your attention.
4. Any interview request that comes out of this week's pitches will be held until after Tuesday, in line with the rule that no one gives an interview before their session.
The one thing I still need from you is confirmation of which spokespeople can be there on Tuesday, so that Laura can set the practice questions to each person's part of the business.

Sincerely,
Michael
Working Session Minutes: {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} Media Relations Program

Held by video call on the morning after Tuesday's spokesperson preparation session at the {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} offices, to take stock of the session and of the first week of outreach, and to agree how the interview requests now coming in will be handled. Notes taken by Michael Morris.
Attendees

items: Michael Morris, Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Laura Bradley, Senior Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Kimberly Le, Communications Analyst, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Melissa Zimmerman, Communications Analyst, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: 1. How the preparation session went

Sandra Mcdaniel reported that the spokespeople found the session useful and were comfortable telling the company's story in their own words, but that two kinds of question caught them out in the practice interviews: questions about growth plans the company is not ready to discuss, and questions that invited them to comment on competitors. Laura Bradley proposed adding short, approved answers for both to the Q&A document, and the group agreed that the spokespeople should work through those answers in a shorter practice session by video before anyone gives an interview.
2. The protocol at the front desk and the sites

The front desk and site reception staff who sat in on the first hour of the session are now working from the v2 protocol, and Sandra said the only question to come back so far is what a site manager should do when a local reporter calls them directly instead of the main line. It was agreed that site managers will take the reporter's name, outlet and deadline and pass them to Sandra the same day, and Laura will add that step to the protocol and reissue it as v3.
3. Outreach, coverage and the check against public statements

Kimberly Le took the group through the first weekly summary, which went out on Friday: several of the trade reporters pitched in the first round have replied, some of them asking for interviews, while coverage naming {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} has been light and neutral and trade coverage across the sector has centered on rising costs and difficulty hiring, which the group agreed are the subjects reporters are most likely to raise in a first interview.

Melissa Zimmerman reported on her check of the Q&A document against her file of the company's public statements over the past year and flagged one passage that describes growth in stronger terms than the company has used before; the group agreed to go back to the earlier wording, and Melissa will also circulate her finished table comparing how peer companies have been covered in the same trade titles.
4. The interview requests

The interview requests from the first round will be scheduled once the spokesperson concerned has done the video practice session and Sandra has signed off on the revised Q&A document, with Laura proposing times to each reporter and Michael Morris sitting in on the first interviews himself. Sandra asked for at least a day's notice before any interview is confirmed, so that she can clear the spokesperson's diary, and the team agreed to treat that as a standing rule for the rest of the program.
Actions agreed

rows: Add approved answers on growth plans and on competitors to the Q&A document and circulate it as v2
Add the site-manager step to the inquiry protocol and reissue it as v3
Circulate the peer coverage table and the revised growth wording
Confirm spokesperson times for a short practice session by video
Sign off on Q&A v2 before any interview is confirmed
Send the weekly summary and flag the same day any story that names {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}}
Prepare a briefing note for the spokesperson ahead of each confirmed interview
Propose interview times to the reporters who have asked, once items 4 and 5 are done

blocks.text: The next working session will be held in two weeks in the same format, or sooner if an interview raises anything that needs a decision from the company.
Status Report: Media Relations Program for {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}}
Prepared by Laura Bradley, Ashcombe Advisory Partners, for the {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} leadership team.
Where the program stands
The program is on track at roughly its halfway point. The first round of outreach is complete, and the first interviews it produced are now on the calendar.
Your spokespeople are prepared and are working from an approved Q&A document. A reporter's call now has a clear route into the company and on to us.
Spending is in line with plan. We cover the budget at the end of this report.
What we completed this period
The first pitches went out in the second week of June. You saw each one in its final form before it reached a reporter, and that will remain the practice.
Much of the rest of the period went into getting your spokespeople ready. We ran the preparation session at your offices, and a shorter practice session by video the following week.
The practice interviews showed us where the answers needed work. We added approved answers on growth plans and on competitors to the Q&A document, and v2 now has your sign-off.
The media inquiry protocol is at v3 and in use at the front desk and at the sites. This version adds a step for site managers who are called directly by a local reporter.

rows: Complete; each pitch reviewed by you before sending
Session at your offices and video practice both held
Growth wording aligned; peer coverage table circulated

blocks.text: Kimberly Le's weekly summary has gone out each Friday since outreach began. Coverage of {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} so far has been light and neutral, which gives the interviews a clean starting point.

Melissa Zimmerman checked the Q&A document against what the company has said publicly over the past year. She found one passage on growth that went further than earlier statements, and we have brought it back in line with them.

Her table of how peer companies have been covered in the same trade titles is now part of the briefing pack. It also shows which reporters already know the sector well, and we will use it to order the second round.
The weeks ahead
Our focus now moves from pitching to interviews. Kimberly Le will prepare a short briefing note for the spokesperson before each one, and Michael Morris will sit in on the first few himself.
The replies to the first round have been encouraging. Reporters' questions so far have been about costs and hiring, as we expected, and the Q&A document covers both.

Each interview request will reach you at least a day before it is confirmed, as we agreed, so there is time to clear the spokesperson's diary. We would also like a brief refresher with each spokesperson beforehand; half an hour by video is usually enough.

Alongside the interviews, we will prepare a second round of pitches to reporters we held back from the first. We will also finish the spokesperson biographies, which reporters tend to ask for once an interview is booked.
What we need from your side
Three things from your team will keep the next few weeks moving. None of them should take long.

items: Holiday dates for each spokesperson through the summer.
Sign-off on the spokesperson biographies when they reach you.
A stand-in at the company for interview requests on days when your usual approver is out of the office.

blocks.text: Risks we are watching

Summer schedules are the main risk to the timetable. If a spokesperson is away when a reporter is ready to talk, the slot may go to another company. Knowing holiday dates early lets us steer requests toward whoever is available.

The second risk is a story that starts somewhere we do not expect. A reporter could still approach a site or a former employee directly. The protocol covers the first case, and Kimberly Le's monitoring should pick up the second early.

The third is drift in the wording. As spokespeople grow comfortable with reporters, they tend to say more than the Q&A allows, especially about growth. Melissa Zimmerman will check each interview against the approved language once it runs.
Budget
The work remains within the agreed fee of {{fact:f:E-2022-001.fee}}. Time spent to date is where we expected it to be at this stage, and we do not expect to ask for any change to the fee.
Your team has moved quickly on every approval, and that has kept each step on schedule. Michael Morris and I would be glad to go through any part of this report on a call.
